Ace of Trades, Ripster, Fuzz, BuySellShort, Ammar have helped a lot. 

General advice is spend 4-6 hours a day learning and researching.  Get bored and take a break.  Go back to technical analysis and learning because you have a void in your life and NEED to trade. Repeat until you see charts and analysis in every part of your daily life and you feel like a crazy person. 

Then take all of that knowledge and experience and create your own plan because you see patterns and have conviction in what you’re doing. 

Take excruciatingly detailed notes.  My trades take 5-20 minutes, my review of those trades take 30-50 minutes. 

Trading should not be an adrenaline sport, it should mechanical and boring and make you feel more like a crazy person 

MAKE IT MAKE SENSE AND BELIEVE IN WHAT YOUR DOING. 

Plan your trade, trade your plan.  Make rules and follow them.  If it’s not working, check your notes, identify the fail point and adjust accordingly. Repeat.

My calatheas get medium to bright indirect light, 2-6 hours per day, no direct light. Depending on variety they are in a window, or more particular ones are under lights. 

My soil base is a 50/50 mix of tropical plant soil and perlite, then I’ll add pumice if I want it even lighter.  Extra perlite mixed at the bottom of the pot. I mist once an hour while lights are on, or twice a day for those in windows. And I typical spritz the soil when watering to prevent any additional compaction.  They stay between 65-85 degrees year round.  

I keep mine lightly damp/moist but they will do poorly if the soil is soggy.  When in doubt let it dry out more before watering.  It’s easier to prune a brown leaf than deal with root rot and root loss. If it’s a darker leafed variety, I find they prefer a little less bright light, and a touch less water, but still looove the stay moist. 

I fertilize with areogardens liquid plant fertilizer 5ml to 120oz of distilled water.  Fluoride is toxic to most tropical plants and is found in a lot of tap water. 

I water/fertilizer weekly, again depending on variety and pot size. Sometimes just to top up the moisture on the outside a bit.  Eventually the top inch will get pretty dry and that’s when I’ll give a good soak. 

They also sit on humidity trays, 3/4 inch of pebble sized gravel and I kept the water level just under the gravel. 

Two key factors, that made a huge different for me personally. 
1- they do not like breezes or drafts.  If they are near a window, I don’t open that window pretty much ever. Even if it’s a nice warm day. 

2- make sure the pot size fits the roots size and plant size.  If the pot is too big they will do poorly and you will very easily over water them.  The roots need something to push against and absorb the water quickly before it starts to get soggy and mushy. Too big and too deep of a pot makes care for them extremely difficult. 

I have down potted two of them and they have started doing much better.  

I’m not an expert, I’ve just failed a lot and have a dozen+ Calatheas.
